critique: The 6×6 puzzle board is correctly the largest and most central element, but the equally weighted help card on the left and storybook-challenge card on the right create two secondary reading branches before the player has understood the route objective. The Cub and star are visually legible inside the grid, yet their meaning is explained only in a small, remote legend at lower left, weakening the label-to-object relationship. The tiny italic footer instruction is easy to miss, while Reset and Run Trail are nearly equal in visual weight despite Run being the intended primary next action.
suggestion: Preserve the board as the hero but reduce the two side cards' contrast and visual mass, consolidating their essential guidance into one quieter instruction tier. Place concise Start and Goal cues adjacent to the Cub and star or directly beneath the board so their meaning is learned at the point of use. Create a single top-to-bottom path from title and chapter objective, to board, to a clearly dominant Run Trail button; make Reset smaller and secondary, and increase the instruction text enough to be read without competing with the board.
